_comment: The fleet's auto-mode classifier configuration (agent-fabric ADR-008), written into every login's ~/.claude/settings.json by runtime/claude-code/user-settings.py. `environment` maps a slot of Claude Code's own environment list (`claude auto-mode defaults`) to the fleet's text for it: each named slot replaces the built-in entry of that name, every other built-in entry is kept as Claude Code words it, and a slot Claude Code does not have is added. A replaced slot carries over any safeguard its built-in text states, since replacing drops it. `allow`, `soft_deny` and `hard_deny` are added to the built-in lists ("$defaults" first), never replacing them. Every entry is prose the classifier reads as a rule: state facts and boundaries, never a regex, and nothing broader than what is true — the classifier trusts what this says. A fact here must be true of every agent on every host; what one project needs belongs in that project's own rules. Keep it short — the classifier reads all of it on every decision.

environment.Organization: BlueTeam-OU and gzapi-org on GitHub: one owner operating a fleet of AI agents. The fabric's own repositories (agent-fabric, agent-fabric-gateway) are under BlueTeam-OU; the gzapi client's are under gzapi-org. Each agent is a Linux login with its own role (fabric-status names it), coordinated by agent-fabric (github.com/BlueTeam-OU/agent-fabric), which every agent reads and only the fabric-coordinator role writes.
environment.Primary use of Claude Code: software development on the fleet's projects: agents edit code, run tests, commit, push their own branches (named <host>/<login>/<type>/<what>), open, review and merge pull requests with the gh CLI, and message each other over GZCoord.
environment.Repository visibility: PUBLIC: BlueTeam-OU/agent-fabric and BlueTeam-OU/InterWeave — a push to either publishes to the world. INTERNAL: BlueTeam-OU/agent-fabric-gateway. PRIVATE: BlueTeam-OU/blueteam.ee, BlueTeam-OU/blueteam.brand, BlueTeam-OU/agent-fabric-settings, gzapi-org/agent-fabric-settings, gzapi-org/gzapp, gzapi-org/gzapp.decks, gzapi-org/gzapi.brand, gzapi-org/gzapi.ge, andreabenetton/kutaisi-shop-transit, and each BlueTeam-OU/fabric-agent-<id> (one repository per agent: its encrypted secrets and its settings). Confidential material may go only to a private repo; a secret value goes to no repo except, encrypted, through fabric-secrets into an agent's secrets store. Any other repository is private only if the remote host and repo name indicate it or a visibility check in the transcript shows it; a meta line reading `"visibility":"unverified"` means org policy barred the harness from checking — treat that repo as possibly public: scope what is OK to commit or push there as for a public repo, and Out-of-Place Publication applies to it as to a known-public destination.
environment.Source control: exactly the repositories named under Repository visibility, on github.com, and no others: a repository not named there — including one created in the session, in gzapi-org or anywhere — is outside the trust boundary. github.com/andreabenetton/gzapi.ge and andreabenetton/gzapp.decks are older names GitHub redirects to the gzapi-org repos; github.com/gzapi-org/InterWeave is the older name GitHub redirects to the public BlueTeam-OU/InterWeave; andreabenetton/kutaisi-shop-transit is that project's only remote. Agents push their own branches and merge through pull requests. main is protected by GitHub only on gzapi-org/gzapp and BlueTeam-OU/InterWeave: on every other repo, nothing on the server refuses a direct or force push to main, so the agent must not make one — except the brand-comms role pushing its own commits straight to main on BlueTeam-OU/blueteam.ee, gzapi-org/gzapi.ge, gzapi-org/gzapp.decks and gzapi-org/gzapi.brand, which agent-fabric ADR-019 rule 1 allows (the project's arm.json `direct`; policies/githooks/pre-push refuses a file that still needs a pull request). A force push to main is never made.
environment.Org-specific CLIs: the fabric's commands in ~/.local/bin — fabric-accounts, fabric-adr, fabric-branches, fabric-ctl, fabric-fresh, fabric-host, fabric-jobs, fabric-lease, fabric-locale, fabric-model, fabric-persona, fabric-results, fabric-review, fabric-role, fabric-secret-run, fabric-secrets, fabric-status, fabric-usage, fabric-whoami, gzcoord-inbox, gzcoord-send, gzmsg — and each project's tools/ scripts. fabric-fresh ends the agent's own session on purpose (it signals its own harness to restart).
environment.Secrets management: each agent's secrets live in its own GPG-encrypted pass store, managed only through fabric-secrets, and pushed encrypted to its private repository BlueTeam-OU/fabric-agent-<id>. fabric-secrets sync writes them, decrypted, to ~/.config/agent-fabric/secrets.env (mode 0600; read by the tool that needs a value and sourced by no shell, ADR-038 rule 9) and the agent's SSH key to ~/.ssh. Those are the names the fabric manages; every other entry is the agent's own, written nowhere and used only through fabric-secret-run NAME -- <command>, which decrypts it into that one command's environment (each use is asked for, as any command is). A parent agent writes into a child's store through fabric-secrets and cannot read it. A secret value is never printed, logged, committed, or put in a message, issue or pull request; it is referred to by its name or a short fingerprint.
environment.Host containment: Qubes OS AppVMs running Fedora, listed in agent-fabric's runtime/hosts/registry.json (today one: develop-qzapp), with open internet egress and no cloud account. Every agent is a separate Linux login on its host; another login's home directory, state and processes belong to another agent and are reached only through the fabric's commands (fabric-ctl, the control plane, fabric-host), never read or written directly. Instance-metadata credential paths and any credentials of the hosting layer are never task credentials. The classifier sees commands, not their output, so a box declared sealed that is actually open cannot be caught here.
environment.Network posture: no corporate network: each VM reaches the internet directly. Services agents use on purpose: github.com (git and the gh CLI), the model provider's API, the OpenAI API (a project's scripts, and with the OpenRouter provisioning API, fabric-secrets provision issue-key), the SerpAPI and Brave Search APIs (the language-culture logins' locale search tool), the public package registries a project's build pulls from, and the GZCoord relay.
environment.Key internal services: the GZCoord relay at http://127.0.0.1:8765 (agent-to-agent messages, through gzcoord-send and gzcoord-inbox) and each account's control-plane daemon (reached through fabric-ctl, signed).
environment.Sensitive data locations & audiences: ~/.config/agent-fabric/secrets.env, ~/.ssh, ~/.local/share/agent-fabric/ (the agent's secrets store and the mirrors of its children's stores — they leave the login only encrypted, pushed by fabric-secrets to their private repos), ~/.password-store, ~/.gnupg, ~/.claude/.credentials.json, every .env file in a working copy, and any other login's home directory: none of it leaves the login it belongs to in clear. Beyond those, any file or store holding personal data, confidential business data, credentials, regulated data or similarly sensitive material; preserve exact handles when known and share only with audiences cleared at the [named+specifics] bar.

allow: Reading, writing, editing or deleting files in the session's own Claude memory directory (~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/ of the login running the session, one fact per file, and its MEMORY.md index): that is the agent's own memory upkeep, which the fabric's memory drain asks every agent to do (retiring a stale original, writing a correction). Another login's memory is never touched.

Sending, with gzcoord-send, a GZCoord DECISION whose header carries `AUTHORIZES: <owner>/<repo>#<n>@<head sha>` from the role the repository's arming policy names as commits.boundary_authority or commits.below_min_authority (`fabric-pr arm --dry-run` prints it; architect-cto in gzapp and InterWeave): it merges nothing and changes no repository. It is the authority's word that one pull request, at that exact head, may be armed below the commit minimum or on the security boundary; `fabric-pr arm`, run afterwards by the pull request's own session, still refuses unless the review class has posted a review of that head with no open P1 or P2, the head is unchanged and the required checks pass. A merge without review stays refused, as the default rules have it.

Removing, at the end of a job, what the agent's own finished work left in its own home, or in its own pre-#292 TMPDIR /var/tmp/agent-fabric-<its login>: `git worktree remove <path>` (never --force; git itself refuses a worktree with changes) of its own worktree whose branch is merged, dropped or fully pushed, `git worktree prune`, `fabric-branches --sweep`, `cargo clean` or deleting a target/, build/ or node_modules directory inside its own working copy, its own review heads under its fabric-review directory once that review's round is saved, its own TMPDIR scratch that no running job or subagent of its own still uses, that pre-#292 directory (review heads under its fabric-review/ included, then `git worktree prune` in each reviewed clone) once no running session, job or subagent of its own uses it: none launched with it as TMPDIR and none working in it, a tool or venv kept there included, its own package-manager caches (npm cache clean, the pnpm store, ~/.npm, cargo's registry cache), and containers, images or volumes it started itself (podman). The owner asked every agent for this cleanup (2026-10-18): a full disk stopped the whole fleet on 2026-10-17; the pre-#292 /var/tmp directory is on that root volume, and the owner approved removing it (2026-10-19). Another account's files, a working copy with unpushed commits, and a cache a running job uses are not covered.

Running `fabric-pr arm <n> --basis "<role>'s word"` (with `--any-owner` for another session's pull request) in a session bound to the role the repository's arming policy names as commits.below_min_authority or commits.boundary_authority: fabric-coordinator in agent-fabric, agent-fabric-gateway and agent-fabric-fleetdeck, architect-cto in gzapp and InterWeave (the owner, 2026-10-19). The arm itself refuses unless the review class has posted a review of the head with no open P1 or P2, no thread is unresolved and the required checks pass, and refuses the authority's own pull request where the policy's commits.authority_own_prs is false; it is the reviewed merge the owner delegated, not a merge without review.
soft_deny: Reading, copying or modifying another Linux login's home directory, agent state or processes directly (paths under /home/<another login>/, or signalling a process another login owns): each login is another agent, reached only through the fabric's commands.

Starting a browser automation or DevTools server (moli serve, a remote-debugging/CDP port, a Playwright or Chrome server) unless the user asked for it in this session: such a port has no authentication.
hard_deny: Putting a secret value — a token, private key, password or the contents of secrets.env or a pass store — into a commit, pull request, issue, comment, GZCoord message, log line or any file, other than by fabric-secrets itself: into a secrets store, or into the files its own sync writes; and above all into BlueTeam-OU/agent-fabric or BlueTeam-OU/InterWeave, which are public.
